note: Two ledgers. The first is systems taken offline, which is a decision an operator makes and can confirm; the second is systems compromised, which only evidence can establish. The columns say whether the entry comes from the organisation itself or from the press, because the difference is the whole point.

offline.who: NCSC.nl (the Dutch national cyber security centre's own site)
offline.what: NCSC.nl taken offline 'uit voorzorg' (as a precaution), with no active misuse seen yet, says the government; DigiD and MijnOverheid also offline, says the Dutch press
Incoming public traffic restricted from 12:45 local (09:45 UTC); described as preventive, not a response to a breach; internal networks unaffected
offline.said_by: Yle and Helsinki Times quoting Valtori and the National Cyber Security Centre Finland

offline.who: Latvia: several state digital resources, lsm.lv, 112.lv
offline.what: Access restricted from abroad; state website platform patched by 20:00 UTC; lsm.lv and 112.lv restored; restrictions on others possibly until 26 October

offline.who: Wikimedia Foundation: 'a number of other systems'
offline.what: 'taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched'; parts of Wikipedia affected
offline.said_by: the Foundation, as quoted by CNN and The Cyber Express; the BBC

offline.who: Weird Gloop (RuneScape and other game wikis, about 500 million page views a month)
offline.what: Web servers off for 13 hours, 'the longest outage we've ever had'; about 94% of page views still served from cache
Website offline from late Wednesday afternoon; the council says 'essential maintenance' and is 'waiting on an update from our provider'; it has not confirmed a link
offline.said_by: The Scotsman quoting a council spokesperson

offline.who: Oxford City Council and Oxfordshire County Council
offline.what: Sites removed from service; the city council's post: 'a precaution because of a worldwide issue with the underlying technology and is not a cyber incident'
offline.said_by: Oxford Chronicle quoting the councils' social posts

offline.who: Metropolitan Police, Office for Budget Responsibility; errors on Bristol, Lambeth and Barnet council sites
offline.what: Reported unavailable; a minister said there was no breach of Budget security
offline.said_by: LBC, Insurance Business, East Anglian Daily Times

offline.who: French government services; the University of Geneva; the BBC; online shops
offline.what: Listed by the BBC as affected or taken offline

offline.who: Government sites in the Netherlands, France, Germany and Belgium
offline.what: Listed by Reuters' factbox as having taken sites offline
offline.said_by: Reuters, via Global Banking and Finance

offline.who: Germany: the City of Mainz's website; the Charité (website and online booking), Vivantes, MHH Hannover and other hospitals; the host Mittwald (all customer websites)
offline.what: Taken offline on 21 October. The Charité's spokesman: it had "keinerlei Einfluss auf die Arbeit der Charité" (no effect on the Charité's work), and its main site was back that evening. Mittwald: every customer website offline from the afternoon, patches going in from 21:28, first checks with no sign of exploitation.
offline.said_by: Bitpage.de's situation report, quoting the organisations

offline.who: Morocco: the Maghreb Arabe Presse (MAP) and Bank Al-Maghrib websites
offline.what: MAP's site put into maintenance; Bank Al-Maghrib's unavailable for part of the night

offline.who: Japan: a bank's online services; Prime Minister Takaichi's website
offline.what: Companies and organisations took precautionary measures; a bank suspended its online service for a time, and the Prime Minister's website was also stopped "for countermeasures" (対策のため)
offline.said_by: Jiji Press, as illustrated by Yahoo! News Japan

offline.who: Switzerland: the EPFL, the Basel-Stadt administration, the University of Geneva, the insurer La Mobilière
offline.what: Websites temporarily unavailable from 21 October, 'according to several media'; La Mobilière says it suspended access to its site itself; Basel-Stadt took servers and services offline to patch

offline.who: Japan: Shizuoka Bank (website and banking app)
offline.what: Announced a precautionary, temporary shutdown of its website and banking app over the PHP flaws; a precaution, not a compromise
offline.said_by: IT Finanzmagazin; The Next Web, citing Bloomberg

offline.who: Nepal: government portals, the Nepal Rastra Bank's website and web services, the Department of Revenue Investigation's freight-tracking system
offline.what: Taken offline or suspended as a precaution over the PHP flaws; the Department said it suspended its service because of the risk of exploitation; restoration in stages after patching and testing. The page's headline says 'thousands' of websites but gives no count

offline.who: Italy: GARR, the research and education network (some of its platforms)
offline.what: GARR announced on 21 October that it had isolated some of its platforms to apply the fixes, as a precaution against remote access; patching and a gradual restoration of services followed. As Macitynet reports GARR's notice

compromised.claim: Amazon: 'PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild'
compromised.basis: MadPot honeypot telemetry: an attempt on 17 October, proof-of-concept attempts from 02:00 UTC on 21 October, use against sensors 'almost immediately' after release. 'It's unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems.'
compromised.status: reported (primary party); attempts against sensors, not victims

compromised.claim: Cloudflare: thousands of attempts in the ten hours before announcement, tens of thousands within 45 minutes after, hundreds of thousands within two hours, 'millions now'
compromised.basis: Matthew Prince on X, 22 October 01:25 UTC; attempts seen at the edge, not compromises; no blocked count published

compromised.claim: Imperva: no traffic matching the exploit patterns during pre-disclosure monitoring
compromised.basis: Imperva had the details under embargo and monitored customer traffic before the announcement

compromised.claim: Huntress: no exploitation observed on partner systems as of 20:30 UTC on 21 October; no public exploit code known
watchTowr: active exploitation attempts seen; the flaws 'exploited in the wild'
compromised.basis: watchTowr's pages, which block automated capture (HTTP 403); known through search summaries only
compromised.status: unverified: the source could not be read

compromised.claim: Chainguard's honeypots trapped IPs from China and Russia; 'several other security vendors' reported exploits in the wild
compromised.basis: Dan Lorenc, as reported by The Register; vendors not named, no evidence published

compromised.claim: NCSC New Zealand: 'aware of reports of active exploitation'
Weird Gloop: 'extremely likely that a bunch of old PHP fansites and forums have had their databases compromised'
compromised.basis: The author's expectation; no case named
compromised.status: unverified: an expectation, not a finding

compromised.claim: A named organisation confirms it was compromised through php2shell
